transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM), Jamal Reed (FinVault Head of Infra), Priya Nair (FinVault SRE), Thomas Wu (FinVault Security)

Summary:
- Quick recap of last week's KB caching change and perf test
- Intermittent 503s during burst tests still appearing, likely routing/NAT related
- Plan for runtime upgrade to v1.4 and a rollback window
- Action items and next steps confirmed

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: morning everyone thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes, quick agenda — updates from us, updates from your infra side, then deep dive into the 503s and upgrade plan.
[00:17] Jamal: yep thanks, catching up here, we did the burst run Friday and saw the blips you mentioned, Priya has logs, I'll let her speak to details.
[00:28] Priya: yeah the 503s show up around 14:12 UTC during the 20k token burst, roughly 2% failure rate, i attached the tail logs into the shared folder but there are a few weird things: source IPs look like the NAT pool sometimes flipping and a couple of TCP RSTs.
[00:45] Samir: thanks, that aligns with what we saw in the agent traces — the requests that hit the fallback path were routed to an older runtime instance that had a full KV cache flush. we're thinking it's a combination of route instability plus our fallback policy triggering.
[01:03] Thomas: from security side curious — does the fallback path leak customer data to other compute? we need guarantees there.
[01:12] Maya: good question, the pilot is configured for tenant isolation but we should show the flow. Avery, Samir want to walk through the isolation model briefly?
[01:24] Avery: sure — Redwood Private uses per-tenant namespaces in the control plane and VPC peering for data plane. the runtime instances are pinned to the customer's subnet when you choose private mode; fallback still stays within the tenant's SGs. sorry if the notes earlier said 'Redwood Privatee' — auto transcript typo — but no cross-tenant exposure.
[01:45] Jamal: that's reassuring, Thomas can follow up on audit logs.
[01:53] Thomas: yes please, we need syslog/audit info for the compliance review.
[02:02] Samir: on the 503s, i ran a trace — see the shared '503-trace-0905.log' — we saw spikes in latency to the NAT gateway, which caused the runtime to mark sessions as failed then trigger the fallback to cold instances. when the NAT gateway re-established, the cache warm-up caused a short burst of failures.
[02:26] Priya: we do rotate NATs during morning maintenance, but this happened during your stress test window which is outside our maint window. i can pull flow logs and share.
[02:35] Avery: actionable then — we need the flow logs + firewall rules so Samir can correlate.
[02:42] Samir: yeah if you can confirm the egress ranges and whether there's any active connection tracking timeout at the NAT it would help. particularly if conntrack is timing out under heavy ephemeral flows.
[02:56] Priya: default conntrack is 30s, but we have modified some timeouts, will confirm.
[03:05] Jamal: another question on routing — we used simple VPC peering but there's a transit gateway in the middle; could that be altering path MTU or doing asymmetric routing?
[03:17] Samir: possible, transit gateways sometimes NAT or change source IP depending on route policies. that's consistent with the 'swapped source IPs' in the logs.
[03:29] Thomas: any security risk with that?
[03:33] Samir: no direct data exposure, but it complicates troubleshooting and sometimes breaks sticky routing which our KV cache relies on for low-latency sessions.
[03:45] Maya: okay on the upgrade to runtime v1.4 — Samir, can you summarize changes and backward compatibility?
[03:52] Samir: v1.4 includes a few fixes: improved KV cache warm-start, better kernel selection for small-batch attention, and a more resilient fallback path that logs reasons for fallback earlier. there are also some network telemetry hooks which will help us surface NAT/conntrack issues. it's backwards compatible with v1.3 models but we recommend a canary window because the kernel selection tweaks can change latencies by a few ms.
[04:19] Priya: will upgrading require downtime or IP changes?
[04:24] Samir: no IP changes; upgrade is rolling with traffic drain on each instance. expected ~2-5 minutes per instance for drain and restart. we'll schedule a maintenance window and provide healthcheck probes to gate the rollout.
[04:39] Jamal: preferred window for us is off-peak 02:00-05:00 UTC, we can do 02:00-04:00 on 2025-09-17 if that works.
[04:50] Avery: noted, we'll propose that slot.
[04:54] Thomas: on observability — can we get span-level tracing for request routing so we can tie a 503 to the network hop?
[05:02] Samir: yes v1.4 exposes distributed traces and link to our console; we'll need to wire an OTLP collector or allow us to push the traces into your existing system — which do you prefer?
[05:12] Priya: we use Honeycomb and have an OTLP endpoint, can share credentials.
[05:17] Samir: perfect, add that to the ticket.
[05:22] Avery: quick note on benchmarks — last week's 95th percentile latency for the heavy prompt profile was 180ms for small-batch, 220ms for burst. after kv warm-up it dropped to ~150ms. these numbers are for the current runtime v1.3 and quantized model q4_8.
[05:42] Jamal: acceptable for now but our SLA target is 150ms p95 for the interactive profile, so we need to narrow that.
[05:50] Samir: a few levers: increase pinned capacity to avoid cold starts, tweak batching config (lower max latency but higher concurrency), and enable prefix caching more aggressively. we can run a tuning pass during the next test window.
[06:07] Priya: how much does pinned capacity cost vs letting autoscale handle it? we want a cost estimate.
[06:14] Avery: i'll include pricing options in the follow-up — quick numbers: reserved capacity reduces per-token cost by ~25% in our examples but depends on utilization. i'll send a spreadsheet.
[06:26] Jamal: please do.
[06:28] Samir: also noticed a couple of model variant fallbacks to a smaller quantized variant which slightly increased latency variance; that's expected under capacity pressure. if you want consistent latency we can prioritize a single variant with dedicated capacity.
[06:46] Thomas: for compliance we also need KMS key attestations — can you share the key management flow for Private?
[06:54] Maya: yes Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and we can provide attestation docs. Avery will share the security pack.
[07:04] Priya: about the 503 RCA — i'll upload flow logs and the NAT config, what format do you want?
[07:09] Samir: raw VPC flow logs (JSON) plus a screenshot of NAT gateway attributes is ideal. we'll parse and correlate.
[07:17] Jamal: any risk to PII during these traces? we sanitize logs but confirm we don't capture full user content.
[07:24] Maya: we don't persist customer request payloads in control plane logs; runtime logs only have metadata by default. full transcripts are not stored unless you opt in.
[07:33] Thomas: ok please include that in the security doc.
[07:38] Avery: recap next steps — Samir runs end-to-end routing test once Priya shares flow logs, Samir will also push a debug trace with v1.4 in canary once we schedule it, Avery will send pricing and security pack, and we'll propose the upgrade window for 2025-09-17 02:00-04:00 UTC.
[07:59] Priya: timeline works — i'll try to get logs by Friday.
[08:05] Jamal: we'll be ready to sign off on upgrade once we see the canary traces and audit logs.
[08:12] Avery: great, anything else?
[08:15] Thomas: just one minor ask — include a short doc on rollback triggers and SLA impact.
[08:21] Samir: will do, rollback triggers will be failures >1% for more than 3 consecutive minutes or repeated healthcheck fails. we'll include details.
[08:33] Avery: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with notes and the action items.
[08:40] Meeting end.

References/Links mentioned:

Avery: Samir to run E2E routing test and share logs by 2025-09-12; Priya to provide NAT/egress config by 2025-09-15; Redwood to schedule v1.4 canary on 2025-09-17 02:00-04:00 UTC; Avery to send pricing/security docs by 2025-09-19.
